key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca$_3$PX$_3$ strongly tunes photovoltaic performance, with Ca$_3$PI$_3$ emerging as the best solar-cell candidate.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a composition-driven route to optimize perovskite absorbers by balancing stability, bandgap, and efficiency for device design.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Band structure and optical analysis across X = F, Cl, Br, I
SLME-based photovoltaic screening for solar-cell suitability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV and SLME results showing Ca$_3$PI$_3$ at 29.6% efficiency versus only 0.6% for Ca$_3$PF$_3$.
watch_item: The results are computational screening outputs, so experimental stability, synthesis feasibility, and device-level losses still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
